topics.topic: Credential-file newline normalization and control-character validation
questions: Does `control character` mean ASCII C0 plus DEL, Unicode general category `Cc`, C0/C1 controls, or another closed set?
What exactly counts as the one removable trailing newline, and what happens with CRLF or multiple trailing newline characters?
Which trailing byte sequence is removed, whether exactly one or all such sequences are removed, and which Unicode or ASCII characters count as control characters?

judgement.why: This is the same credential newline, control-character and encoding question already judged in P1, and the relevant passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Credential newline normalization, control-character rules, and HTTP byte encoding
precedent.why: The exact newline sequence, character repertoire, and HTTP wire encoding are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Unit used for disclosed non-open failure-detail length
questions: Which length is disclosed for a non-open `failure_detail`?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
Is the disclosed failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or another unit?

judgement.why: This is the same failure-detail length-unit question already judged in P4, and the relevant passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Unit and truncation basis for disclosed failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later note specifies the UTF-8 byte length of the retained failure_detail.

topics.topic: Valid credential HTTP-header values and non-ASCII wire serialization
questions: Which credential characters are valid, and how is a valid non-ASCII value serialized into an HTTP header?
Are non-ASCII credential values allowed, and if so, how are they encoded into the HTTP header field value?
Which credential values are valid HTTP field values, and how are accepted non-ASCII characters and surrounding whitespace represented on the wire?

judgement.why: This is the same credential character grammar, whitespace and HTTP wire-encoding question already judged in P17, and the relevant passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Credential value character grammar, control characters, whitespace, and wire encoding
precedent.why: The exact newline sequence, character repertoire, and HTTP wire encoding are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Behavior when the selected manifest instance name is absent
questions: Does an absent selected instance name prevent startup, count as no selected instance, or remain a selection whose requests fail for a missing address?

What happens when configuration names an instance that does not exist in the configured manifest revision: does the kernel refuse startup, treat the service as having no selected instance, or fail only requests to that service?

quotes:
`capability:bindings.check_installed_instances`: no credential header has,
   case-insensitively, the name of a required header of its instance or of a
   header the kernel sets itself, `host` included (A09 rule    1). The services checked are those the installation holds a credential for, in
   `service_id` order; for one it also selects an instance for, a manifest
   record that cannot be read or fails a check of the record itself (A08 rule
   5) stops the start naming it; a selected instance
   the record does not list fails nothing here
   (it is not invocable at send, A09 rule 6).
judgement.why: The later startup flow says an absent selected-instance name does not prevent startup and makes the service uninvocable at send.

topics.topic: Credential-leak prevention for service-returned or encoded credential data
questions: Must all representations of a credential be excluded from answers, or is the State 0 promise limited to values the kernel inserts and verbatim echoes it can recognize?
Must the kernel prevent encoded forms of a credential from reaching an answer, or is only a verbatim credential occurrence forbidden?

quotes:
**Secrets** — service credentials and tokens live in the installation's
  protected configuration; they never enter a function, a flow, a trace or an
  answer.

A service's own answer is not the
   kernel's text: a body that echoes the value verbatim, 2xx or not, is
   withheld and never used as an output (A09 rule 7); one that carries it in
   another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class.
judgement.why: State 0 unconditionally excludes credentials from answers, while A17 permits an unrecognized encoded representation to be handled and disclosed according to its class.

topics.topic: Disclosure classification for inputless executions and trial cases
questions: What disclosure class does an inputless execution have for purposes such as redacting its `failure_detail`?
What disclosure class do expected outputs and trial-execution outputs receive for a trial case with no inputs?
What is the execution class, and therefore the class of its failure_detail, when an execution has no inputs?

quotes: highest_disclosure_class: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return the highest member of classes by the declared order of = models.DisclosureClass (open, then business_confidential, then personal_data) and open when classes is empty; no input ever lowers the result.

- **Classes of stored values and spooled files.** The module that writes a
  StoredValue M21 or a SpooledFile M22 sets its class, by one rule (A07 rule 3)
  computed with `canonical_values.highest_disclosure_class`: `flows` for
  constants (the class the composing agent declared, A07 rule 2), `runs` for
  flow inputs (the port's class) and for function outputs, values and files
  alike (the highest class received), `effects` for service outputs, values and
  files alike (the binding's declared class), `functions` for trial cases and
  trial outputs (a case input, authored or captured, the class its contract
  input port declares; an expected output and a trial output, the highest class
  of the case's inputs; M21).

handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
judgement.why: The later texts route execution, expected-output and trial-output classification through a helper that returns open for an empty class collection.

topics.topic: Ordering of non-executable-node propagation versus ready-node execution
questions: When a request simultaneously has ready nodes and nodes that can now be concluded `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`, which conclusions are recorded first and how are they interleaved with executable nodes?

After a conclusion simultaneously makes some nodes non-executable and other nodes ready, must the kernel exhaust skip/upstream-failure propagation before selecting the next ready node, or execute ready nodes first?

judgement.why: This is the same ordering question for newly forced skip or upstream-failure conclusions versus executable nodes already judged in P3, and the relevant passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Ordering and wave semantics for forced conclusions versus executable nodes
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined, executions sorted by (node_id, map_index), with status running; after an operation element, whose concluding record effects wrote, the next RecordRunProgressChange holds the records it made non-executable.
precedent.why: The later run contract requires newly determined skipped and upstream-failed records to be written immediately after the element that determined them, before the advancement loop selects another executable node.

topics.topic: Precedence and reported failure among startup validation checks
questions: In what fixed order are A17-related startup checks performed and which failure is reported first?
When several startup conditions fail, which check is performed and reported first?

quotes: run_start_sequence: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call, in exactly this order and each exactly once: load_installation with config_path; check_installed_instances with the loaded Installation; open_store with that Installation's data_directory; probe_sandbox; recover_in_flight_attempts; recover_running_runs (A03 rule 8, A09 rule 1, A14 rule 5, A18).

run_start_sequence: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Every step is required: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller with the step named in its reason; no later step runs and nothing is retried or skipped.

read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not a regular file or is a symbolic link (checked without following links), is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name.
judgement.why: The later contracts fix both the order among startup modules and the order of checks inside configuration loading, with the first failure reported.

topics.topic: Repeating security checks when rereading the token-list configuration
questions: When the token list is re-read after startup, are A17's no-symlink, ownership, regular-file and permission checks repeated?
When the configuration is reread for token changes, must the kernel repeat A17's ownership, mode, regular-file, and no-symlink checks, and what happens when one fails?

judgement.why: This is the same live configuration re-read question already judged in P21, and the relevant passages have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Revalidation of configuration-file protections during token-list reload
quotes:
Before evaluating each request the kernel reads the configuration file and
   compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ,
   or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it (K-15) and takes from it only the
   token list.

Exactly four checks apply to a re-read: the
   file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two
   tokens are equal; no two agent tokens share a name (M28).

Every other field of the configuration, and every other start check, applies
   only at a restart.
precedent.why: The live re-read applies exactly the four listed token checks, while the file-protection start checks apply only at restart.

topics.topic: Agent-visible representation of partially personal mapped file lists
questions: When a mapped file list is `personal_data` because only some elements are personal, what exactly may an agent see for the list and its open elements?

topics.topic: Credential-header collision checking without a valid selected instance
questions: How is the required startup collision check performed when the manifest cannot yield a valid selected instance?

topics.topic: Disclosure-class propagation through guarded control flow
questions: Does the disclosure class of a guard value taint the guarded delivery, its skip/production result, or the downstream values whose presence it controls?

topics.topic: Handling plaintext personal data submitted by agents
questions: Is the personal-data guarantee only about values returned by the kernel, or must requests from agents containing plaintext `personal_data` be refused?

topics.topic: Mapped-element statuses that are terminal versus retry-eligible
questions: Which NodeExecution statuses make a mapped element terminal, and which merely conclude an attempt while leaving the element eligible for another attempt?

topics.topic: Mapped-output size enforcement when all consuming edges are guard-disabled
questions: Can an oversized mapped list fail the node when every edge that could carry that output is disabled by its guard?

topics.topic: Output processing order and file retention when another output is invalid
questions: If one returned output is invalid and another is a valid file, is that file written and retained as unnamed spool data, and what fixed port and element order decides this?

topics.topic: Persisting the mapped-output size ceiling across restarts and upgrades
questions: Which stored fact fixes the ceiling used to derive this failure after restart or upgrade, so the run and trace cannot be reinterpreted differently by a later release?

topics.topic: Possible-class computation for empty mapped-operation outputs
questions: How must proof compute the possible class of a mapped operation output so an empty mapped input cannot produce a class above the downstream input's accepted class?

topics.topic: Reported status and details for oversized aggregate mapped output
questions: What exact status, reason, and failure detail do run and trace readers report for this derived mapped-node failure, given that no NodeExecution records it?

topics.topic: Scope of approval-preview redaction when any input is personal
questions: When any input is personal, does "only" replace just the built-request representation, or the entire preview including operation metadata and non-personal inputs?

topics.topic: Starting index for mapped elements
questions: What `map_index` is assigned to the first mapped element?

topics.topic: Timing of receiving-port validation
questions: Is target validation performed and recorded as each edge delivers, potentially before other inputs arrive, or only after all inputs are present and the node is selected?

topics.topic: Valid MCP listen addresses and startup failure behavior
questions: What forms of listen address are valid, and does an invalid or unbindable address refuse startup under a defined condition?

topics.topic: Validation order and failure selection for multiple invalid node inputs
questions: When values for several input ports violate their target ports, in what order are they checked and which violation supplies the recorded failure detail?

topics.topic: Whether skipped-by-guard conclusions count as successful run completion
questions: Does `skipped_by_guard` count as a successful conclusion for both nodes and flow outputs when determining the final run status?

topics.topic: Whether waiting elements can execute during ordinary advancement
questions: Can an element waiting for approval, service availability, or unknown-outcome resolution execute during ordinary advancement before the event that ends its wait?
